# ThroughLine rewind capability CHANGELOG v1.3.0

<!-- version-bundle:begin (generated by scripts/version-bundle.ts; edit Version-Record.json, not this block) -->

## 1.3.0 — versioned 0.0.60 rewind carry — 2026-10-10

Version 1.3.0 records the ten protected-path changes carried between 0.0.56 and the 0.0.60 preserve-base release, which shipped under a single-use version exception; upstream reconciliation must preserve the existing same-session rewind behavior and all pinned regression cases.

## 1.2.0 — rewind keeps the same Claude session, like the CLI — 2026-10-02

Rewind no longer forks the Claude transcript. It resumes the same native session cut before the chosen message, so every message id stays the same and rewinds repeat as many times as the operator wants. A rewind to the first message keeps the session too.

- The Claude adapter resumes the same session with resumeSessionAt set to the entry before the chosen message, instead of forkSession plus boundary remapping. The fork-ancestry repair from 1.1.0 is not carried; its identity module and nine cases leave the manifest.
- A first-message rewind cuts at the session-start entry the prompt hangs from, read from the native transcript by the owned helper apps/server/src/throughline/rewind/claudeTranscriptParent.ts. With nothing before it, the rewind refuses and changes nothing.
- The cut stays in the resume cursor until the next reply, so a restart before the next prompt cannot undo the rewind.
- Five new pinned adapter cases; two fork-only cases removed. Probes against Claude Code 2.1.286 confirmed same session id across three repeated rewinds and a first-message rewind.

Evidence: `/Users/Admin/core-root/vault/01_Projects/workbench/infra/t3code/_meta/rewind-same-session-2026-10-02`

## 1.1.0 — exact native ancestry for repeated rewind — 2026-10-02

Retained displayed messages resolve to their current Claude native UUID through recorded fork ancestry. This is the bounded ancestry-only repair; installed behavior remains unproven until release and cold repeated-rewind proof.

- The existing Claude adapter asks the shared fork-owned provider identity module only when direct original UUID and exact turn-ID fallback are absent. No text matching or positional offsets.
- Three owned identity paths added to existing capability protection; nine identity cases pinned by exact name. Existing thirty protected paths and fourteen cases remain.
- Source and SDK review found no defect; source tests and actual SDK forks passed. No live-adapter, native UI or installed acceptance is claimed.
- Fix release 0.0.52 explicitly preserves the admitted previous-release plus existing carry base; the upstream upgrade remains a separate release.

## 1.0.0 — rewind becomes a protected capability — 2026-09-28

The working /rewind of ThroughLine 0.0.50 becomes a named, versioned capability: 30 fork paths tagged in the seam file, 14 fork-authored test cases pinned by name, and a manifest the ship tool reads to stop upstream conflicts, fail a release that loses a pinned case, refuse an unversioned change, and prove rewind live on a throwaway thread.

- History carried in: fork commit faf8ba84fc (release 0.0.49, WCC-127) added the /rewind and /config menus on desktop and phone, the thread.conversation.revert-to-message command, the exact-message Claude fork and the projections that keep earlier history.
- History carried in: fork commit 7b47de72f8 (release 0.0.50) made the Claude adapter admit a fork that dropped an early message after a compaction summary, and still refuse a marker outside the matching stretch. Ryan confirmed rewind works on 0.0.50 on Sep 28, 2026.
- Capability.json written: 30 paths from those two commits, 14 pinned cases, rule "keep the fork's behavior; adopt upstream types around it"; the rewind source files are byte-identical in release 0.0.51.
- Ship-Seams.json: all 30 entries tagged capability rewind (tag check PASS).
- Protections built in Tier 1 (throughline-ship 0.2.0, agent-instruments 0.38.0), reviewed PASS by gate-tlval-74564878, not yet shipped: conflict stop, rewind-regression gate, version rule, live proof, proof-only verbs.
